source_title: Nationwide Ground Stop: Questions and Answers
evidence_description: Opening statement; questions on cause, cyberattack and cancellations. The agency dates the start of technical disruption to about 15:30 Eastern Time on 13 November and says air traffic resumed at 20:15. It describes telecommunications instability during maintenance, reports no indication of a cyberattack in information then available, and says investigation of the underlying cause continued. It reports about 12,462 cancellations that day and explicitly says some were not directly caused by the ground stop.
investigation_relevance: Tier 1. PF(H,E)=0. The agency publishes a bounded account. No named observer is bound in this source. Await the final incident report and a count attributable to the ground stop.

source_authority: United States Department of Transportation · Sean P. Duffy

evidence_description: Attributed statement on the status of the airspace. Secretary Duffy announced that the airspace reopened at 20:15 Eastern Time and said flight recovery would depend on available crews.
relevant_quotation: At 8:15 tonight, Eastern Time, we've opened up the airspace.
investigation_relevance: Tier 1. PF(H,E)=1, Factual Strength FS-MEDIUM for the attributed record. Qualification applies to the named, contemporaneous announcement. Reopening is a separate milestone from restoration of individual flights.
